label: L=3 sequences, first copy step after <DEL> (t=4, outputting orig(1))
explanation: Fires only at one position: step t=4 in length-3 sequences, the step right after <DEL>, where the input is orig(0) and the output is orig(1). It never fires at any other step or for any other L. In dev it fires on about 59% of those steps (recall 1.0, precision 0.59). Which of these steps fire is only weakly tied to token identity: sequences with digit tokens fire less (n_digits=0 holds 71% of mass, n_digits>=2 is rare), and the strongest activations have orig(0)=v and orig(1)/orig(2) among f, d, q, w. Neither restricting to letters nor to digit-free sequences improved F1. Magnitude is small (max 0.056), and no simple variable explains it beyond those weak token preferences.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: v, l, r, b, j, 2; least: g, u, 0, 3) and the second original token (most: p, b, w, f, d, k; least: c, i, y, j); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, L=3, t=4.
